questions.prompt: Which learning area is most directly concerned with acting, directing, staging, and screen performance?
options: Performing Arts
Metalwork
Home Science
Geography
questions.correctAnswer: Performing Arts
questions.explanation: Performing Arts studies live and recorded performance forms such as theatre, spoken word, dance, and film practice.
questions.subStrandTitle: Meaning and Scope of Performing Arts
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the scope of Performing Arts in senior school.

questions.prompt: Which person interprets a script and guides actors, movement, pacing, and stage meaning?
options: Director
Ticket clerk
Audience member
Printer
questions.correctAnswer: Director
questions.explanation: A director shapes the production by guiding performance choices and coordinating the artistic interpretation of the script.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify key roles in a theatre or film production team.

questions.prompt: What is a script in theatre and film?
options: A written plan of dialogue, action, and performance directions
A list of school furniture only
A camera battery label
A costume storage box
questions.correctAnswer: A written plan of dialogue, action, and performance directions
questions.explanation: A script records what performers say and do, giving a production a clear structure before rehearsal or filming.
questions.learningOutcome: Define a script as a foundation for performance creation.

questions.prompt: Which term refers to the people watching a live performance?
options: Audience
Cast list
Props table
Editing suite
questions.correctAnswer: Audience
questions.explanation: The audience receives and responds to the performance, helping complete the communication process in theatre.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the role of the audience in performance.

questions.prompt: Which item is an example of a prop in a school play?
options: A letter carried by a character
The whole audience
The school timetable
The director's idea only
questions.correctAnswer: A letter carried by a character
questions.explanation: A prop is an object handled or used by performers to support action and meaning on stage or screen.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify props used in performance.

questions.prompt: What is dialogue in a play or film?
options: Words spoken by characters
Seats arranged for guests
The colour of curtains
A list of camera prices
questions.correctAnswer: Words spoken by characters
questions.explanation: Dialogue is the spoken exchange between characters and is used to reveal action, relationships, and conflict.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify dialogue as a basic element of dramatic writing.

questions.prompt: Which term means a performer's planned position and movement on stage?
options: Blocking
Budgeting
Cropping
Printing
questions.correctAnswer: Blocking
questions.explanation: Blocking organises where performers stand, enter, exit, and move so that the action is clear to the audience.
questions.learningOutcome: Define blocking in stage performance.

questions.prompt: Which person usually performs a role in front of the camera or audience?
options: Actor
Accountant only
Lighting cable
Poster frame
questions.correctAnswer: Actor
questions.explanation: An actor uses voice, body, imagination, and interaction to portray a character in a performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the performer role in theatre and film.

questions.prompt: Which film shot shows a person or object from very near to highlight detail or emotion?
options: Close-up shot
Wide establishing shot
Aerial map
Blank frame
questions.correctAnswer: Close-up shot
questions.explanation: A close-up directs attention to facial expression, a hand movement, or an important object.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise basic camera shot types used in film.

questions.prompt: What is rehearsal in Performing Arts?
options: Practising a performance before presentation
Selling tickets after the show
Painting a wall with no plan
Deleting the script
questions.correctAnswer: Practising a performance before presentation
questions.explanation: Rehearsal allows performers and production teams to refine timing, movement, voice, and interpretation before presentation.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of rehearsal in performance preparation.

questions.prompt: Which theatre space has audience members mainly facing the stage from one side?
options: Proscenium stage
Editing room
Costume rack
Storage cabinet
questions.correctAnswer: Proscenium stage
questions.explanation: A proscenium arrangement separates stage and audience with the audience viewing mainly from the front.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common theatre performance spaces.

questions.prompt: Which document shows planned camera shots before filming begins?
options: Storyboard
Attendance register
Receipt book
Wardrobe label
questions.correctAnswer: Storyboard
questions.explanation: A storyboard arranges key shots in sequence so the film team can plan framing, action, and transitions.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify a storyboard as a planning tool for film.

questions.prompt: What is characterisation in drama?
options: Creating and presenting a believable character
Counting the number of chairs
Printing a programme cover only
Turning off all lights
questions.correctAnswer: Creating and presenting a believable character
questions.explanation: Characterisation combines voice, movement, dialogue, costume, motivation, and relationships to build a role.
questions.learningOutcome: Define characterisation in dramatic performance.

questions.prompt: Which term refers to the problem or struggle that drives dramatic action?
options: Conflict
Curtain size
Lens cap
Ticket price
questions.correctAnswer: Conflict
questions.explanation: Conflict creates tension and motivates characters to make choices that move the story forward.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify conflict as an element of dramatic structure.

questions.prompt: Which performance form uses rhythm, gesture, voice, and poetic language to present ideas before an audience?
options: Spoken word poetry
Ledger balancing
Soil testing
Circuit drawing
questions.correctAnswer: Spoken word poetry
questions.explanation: Spoken word poetry is designed for oral performance and often uses voice, rhythm, gesture, and imagery.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise spoken word as a performance form.

questions.prompt: Why is voice projection important in live theatre?
options: It helps the audience hear words clearly without strain
It replaces the need for character motivation
It makes costumes unnecessary
It prevents actors from moving
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the audience hear words clearly without strain
questions.explanation: Projection supports clear communication by carrying the voice to the audience while protecting the performer's throat.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of voice projection in live performance.

questions.prompt: Why should a performer warm up before rehearsal or presentation?
options: To prepare the voice and body for safe expressive work
To avoid reading the script
To make the audience leave early
To remove all stage directions
questions.correctAnswer: To prepare the voice and body for safe expressive work
questions.explanation: Warm-ups reduce strain, focus attention, and prepare breathing, articulation, and movement for performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe preparation practices for performers.

questions.prompt: Why is a play's setting important to performers and designers?
options: It gives time, place, and social context for performance choices
It deletes the need for actors
It guarantees a larger audience
It replaces dialogue with silence
questions.correctAnswer: It gives time, place, and social context for performance choices
questions.explanation: Setting guides costume, language, set design, movement, and the mood of the scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how setting influences performance creation.

questions.prompt: How does costume help an audience understand a character?
options: It suggests status, culture, occupation, period, or personality
It removes all need for acting choices
It makes every character identical
It controls camera memory
questions.correctAnswer: It suggests status, culture, occupation, period, or personality
questions.explanation: Costume communicates visual clues that support character, setting, and dramatic meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how costume contributes to character and meaning.

questions.prompt: Why is improvisation useful during early performance creation?
options: It helps performers explore ideas, characters, and action before fixing a script
It replaces all rehearsal discipline
It makes planning impossible
It removes audience response
questions.correctAnswer: It helps performers explore ideas, characters, and action before fixing a script
questions.explanation: Improvisation encourages creativity and discovery, giving material that can later be shaped into a structured performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of improvisation in developing performance material.

questions.prompt: Why does a film team use an establishing shot near the start of a scene?
options: To show the location and context before closer action
To hide all characters permanently
To replace the script with a poster
To record sound without pictures
questions.correctAnswer: To show the location and context before closer action
questions.explanation: An establishing shot helps viewers understand where the scene takes place and how characters relate to the space.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of establishing shots in film scenes.

questions.prompt: What does pace control in a spoken word performance?
options: The speed and rhythm with which ideas are delivered
The price of the microphone
The size of the stage curtain
The number of printed tickets
questions.correctAnswer: The speed and rhythm with which ideas are delivered
questions.explanation: Pace affects emphasis, suspense, clarity, and emotional impact during oral performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe how pace affects spoken word performance.

questions.prompt: Why should a stage manager keep a prompt copy of the script?
options: To track cues, entrances, exits, and technical notes during production
To replace the director in every artistic decision
To hide the play from actors
To record exam marks
questions.correctAnswer: To track cues, entrances, exits, and technical notes during production
questions.explanation: A prompt copy helps coordinate the performance so performers and technical teams work in sequence.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain documentation used in managing a theatre production.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains theme in a play or film?
options: The central idea or issue explored through the story
The height of the stage only
The camera brand used by the crew
The number of seats in the hall
questions.correctAnswer: The central idea or issue explored through the story
questions.explanation: Theme is the deeper idea, concern, or message developed through plot, character, conflict, and images.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain theme as a dramatic element.

questions.prompt: Why is continuity important when filming a scene in several shots?
options: It keeps action, costume, props, and screen direction consistent
It forces all shots to be identical wide shots
It removes the need for editing
It prevents actors from learning lines
questions.correctAnswer: It keeps action, costume, props, and screen direction consistent
questions.explanation: Continuity helps viewers believe the scene is unfolding smoothly even when shots are recorded separately.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of continuity in film production.

questions.prompt: How does lighting support a stage scene?
options: It controls visibility, mood, focus, and time of day
It writes dialogue for the actors
It replaces rehearsal notes
It prints the programme
questions.correctAnswer: It controls visibility, mood, focus, and time of day
questions.explanation: Lighting is both practical and expressive because it helps the audience see and interpret the action.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain functions of lighting in stage performance.

questions.prompt: Why should performers respect cultural sources when adapting a Kenyan oral narrative?
options: To preserve meaning and avoid misrepresentation of community heritage
To make the story impossible to perform
To remove all local language references
To copy without understanding
questions.correctAnswer: To preserve meaning and avoid misrepresentation of community heritage
questions.explanation: Respectful adaptation recognises the value of cultural knowledge while shaping it responsibly for a new audience.
questions.subStrandTitle: Traditional Kenyan Theatre and Oral Narratives
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ethical use of cultural material in performance creation.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of feedback after a rehearsal run-through?
options: To identify strengths and areas to improve before presentation
To embarrass performers instead of helping them grow
To cancel all creative decisions automatically
To replace the audience with a checklist
questions.correctAnswer: To identify strengths and areas to improve before presentation
questions.explanation: Constructive feedback helps the group refine performance choices, timing, clarity, and teamwork.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of constructive feedback during rehearsal.

questions.prompt: Why is teamwork essential in theatre and film production?
options: Many creative and technical roles must coordinate to present one performance
Only one person can do every task at once
It removes all personal responsibility
It makes planning unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: Many creative and technical roles must coordinate to present one performance
questions.explanation: Performers, designers, technicians, managers, and directors depend on one another for a coherent production.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain collaboration as a core value in Performing Arts.

questions.prompt: How does a low camera angle often affect the viewer's impression of a character?
options: It can make the character appear powerful or dominant
It always makes the character invisible
It removes facial expression
It turns the shot into a written script
questions.correctAnswer: It can make the character appear powerful or dominant
questions.explanation: Camera angle influences meaning; looking up at a character can suggest power, confidence, or threat.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how camera angle can shape character meaning.

questions.prompt: Why should a performer listen carefully to other actors on stage?
options: To respond truthfully and maintain believable interaction
To wait for the audience to write the script
To ignore cues deliberately
To avoid character relationships
questions.correctAnswer: To respond truthfully and maintain believable interaction
questions.explanation: Active listening helps actors react in time, keep the scene alive, and support ensemble performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain active listening as a performance skill.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains mise-en-scene in film?
options: The arrangement of setting, costume, lighting, props, and performers in a shot
The price of cinema tickets
The microphone volume only
The number of files on a computer
questions.correctAnswer: The arrangement of setting, costume, lighting, props, and performers in a shot
questions.explanation: Mise-en-scene describes the visible elements placed before the camera to create meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe mise-en-scene as part of screen meaning.

questions.prompt: Why should a performance review include evidence from the production?
options: It supports judgement with specific examples from acting, design, or direction
It makes the review longer without meaning
It allows the reviewer to avoid watching
It turns the review into a ticket
questions.correctAnswer: It supports judgement with specific examples from acting, design, or direction
questions.explanation: Evidence makes a review fair and useful because claims are linked to observable performance choices.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of evidence in performance critique.

questions.prompt: Why are entrances and exits planned during blocking?
options: They organise how characters join and leave action clearly
They prevent characters from speaking
They replace the plot
They make the stage unsafe
questions.correctAnswer: They organise how characters join and leave action clearly
questions.explanation: Clear entrances and exits support story flow, spacing, cue timing, and audience understanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why stage movement needs planning.

questions.prompt: What does editing mainly do in a film production?
options: Selects and arranges recorded shots into a coherent sequence
Builds the school hall stage
Acts every role in the film
Designs all costumes before writing
questions.correctAnswer: Selects and arranges recorded shots into a coherent sequence
questions.explanation: Editing shapes rhythm, continuity, meaning, and story by organising shots and sound after recording.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the role of editing in film storytelling.

questions.prompt: Why is articulation important in speech performance?
options: It makes words distinct and easier for listeners to understand
It changes a stage into a cinema
It hides the theme
It removes all emotional expression
questions.correctAnswer: It makes words distinct and easier for listeners to understand
questions.explanation: Clear articulation helps audiences follow meaning, especially in large spaces or fast-paced scenes.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain articulation as a speech performance skill.

questions.prompt: How can sound effects support a scene set during heavy rain?
options: They help create atmosphere and make the setting believable
They prove the actors know all lines
They replace character motivation
They remove the need for audience focus
questions.correctAnswer: They help create atmosphere and make the setting believable
questions.explanation: Sound effects can suggest weather, place, time, and offstage action when used appropriately.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how sound supports dramatic atmosphere.

questions.prompt: Why should a production team prepare a realistic budget?
options: To plan resources, control costs, and avoid waste
To make rehearsals impossible
To replace creative choices with random spending
To hide expenses from the team
questions.correctAnswer: To plan resources, control costs, and avoid waste
questions.explanation: Budgeting helps a production use available money responsibly for costumes, props, publicity, transport, and technical needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why budgeting matters in performance production.

questions.prompt: Why is copyright important when using a published play or recorded music in a performance?
options: It protects creators' rights and guides lawful use of their work
It allows anyone to claim ownership of another person's work
It prevents original writing by learners
It removes the need to credit sources
questions.correctAnswer: It protects creators' rights and guides lawful use of their work
questions.explanation: Copyright encourages ethical creative practice by recognising ownership, permission, and fair use conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain copyright as an ethical issue in Performing Arts.

questions.prompt: How does a tableau communicate meaning on stage?
options: Performers freeze in a carefully arranged image that shows a moment or idea
Performers leave the theatre before the story begins
The camera records only empty chairs
The audience writes the dialogue aloud
questions.correctAnswer: Performers freeze in a carefully arranged image that shows a moment or idea
questions.explanation: A tableau uses stillness, levels, facial expression, and spacing to focus audience attention on a key meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe tableau as a non-verbal performance technique.

questions.prompt: A group is adapting a folktale about greed for a school audience. Which first step best supports responsible creation?
options: Identify the source, main lesson, characters, and cultural context before scripting
Copy random jokes from online videos
Ignore the meaning of the original story
Begin with expensive costumes before reading
questions.correctAnswer: Identify the source, main lesson, characters, and cultural context before scripting
questions.explanation: Understanding source material helps learners adapt it respectfully while keeping the story's purpose clear.
questions.subStrandTitle: Traditional Kenyan Theatre and Oral Narratives
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsible adaptation steps to oral narrative material.

questions.prompt: A scene feels flat because every line is spoken at the same speed and volume. Which performance choice should be improved?
options: Vocal variation
Ticket numbering
Stage sweeping only
Camera storage
questions.correctAnswer: Vocal variation
questions.explanation: Changing pace, pitch, pause, stress, and volume helps communicate emotion and meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply vocal techniques to improve dramatic delivery.

questions.prompt: A director wants to show that one character controls a meeting. Which blocking choice best supports this idea?
options: Place the character at the centre or head position while others face them
Hide the character behind the audience throughout
Make all actors turn away from the action
Remove every entrance and exit
questions.correctAnswer: Place the character at the centre or head position while others face them
questions.explanation: Stage position and focus can communicate power relationships without adding extra dialogue.
questions.learningOutcome: Use blocking to communicate character relationships.

questions.prompt: Learners are filming a conversation between two characters. Which shot pattern best helps viewers follow who is speaking?
options: Shot-reverse-shot between the two characters
Random shots of feet only
One long shot of an empty wall
A black screen with no sound
questions.correctAnswer: Shot-reverse-shot between the two characters
questions.explanation: Shot-reverse-shot alternates views of speakers and is commonly used to show conversation clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic shot sequencing to film dialogue scenes.

questions.prompt: A spoken word performer wants to emphasise the phrase 'clean water for every home'. Which technique is most suitable?
options: Pause before the phrase and stress its key words
Rush through the phrase quietly
Turn away and mumble every word
Skip the phrase during performance
questions.correctAnswer: Pause before the phrase and stress its key words
questions.explanation: Pause and stress draw attention to important ideas and help the audience remember the message.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply vocal emphasis to communicate a spoken word message.

questions.prompt: A production has no money for a realistic shop set. Which design choice is most practical for a school performance?
options: Use selected signs, counters, and props to suggest the shop
Cancel the play because there is no full building
Use dangerous borrowed furniture without checking it
Ask actors to explain every missing object
questions.correctAnswer: Use selected signs, counters, and props to suggest the shop
questions.explanation: Suggestive set design can create place clearly while staying affordable, safe, and flexible.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply resourceful set design to a school performance context.

questions.prompt: A character enters after receiving bad news but the actor smiles throughout. Which acting element needs stronger attention?
options: Emotional truth and motivation
Ticket sales
Camera charging
Poster spelling only
questions.correctAnswer: Emotional truth and motivation
questions.explanation: The performer should align facial expression, movement, and voice with the character's situation and intention.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply motivation to create believable character behaviour.

questions.prompt: A film scene changes from a classroom to a football field. Which transition is most direct and clear?
options: Cut from the classroom action to an establishing shot of the field
Repeat the same classroom close-up for five minutes
Delete all location clues
Use only a blank title with no image
questions.correctAnswer: Cut from the classroom action to an establishing shot of the field
questions.explanation: An establishing shot after a cut quickly orients viewers to the new location.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply transitions to communicate a change of place in film.

questions.prompt: During rehearsal, two actors keep speaking over each other's important lines. Which solution best improves clarity?
options: Mark cues and practise listening for the end of each line
Increase the number of props in the scene
Move the audience further away
Remove all pauses from the script
questions.correctAnswer: Mark cues and practise listening for the end of each line
questions.explanation: Cue awareness and listening help actors time responses so the audience can follow the dialogue.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply cue discipline to improve ensemble performance.

questions.prompt: A scene about a night guard must look dim but still visible. Which lighting choice is best?
options: Use low-intensity focused light rather than complete darkness
Switch off every light for the whole scene
Shine bright light directly into the audience's eyes
Use only daylight in a closed room
questions.correctAnswer: Use low-intensity focused light rather than complete darkness
questions.explanation: Stage lighting must balance mood with visibility so the audience can see important action safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply lighting choices to communicate mood and maintain visibility.

questions.prompt: A group wants to devise a scene about responsible use of social media. Which process is most suitable?
options: Research the issue, improvise scenarios, select strong moments, then script and rehearse
Film random clips with no message
Copy another school's entire performance
Start publicity before deciding the topic
questions.correctAnswer: Research the issue, improvise scenarios, select strong moments, then script and rehearse
questions.explanation: Devising grows from research, exploration, selection, structuring, rehearsal, and refinement.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply devising steps to create a performance on a contemporary issue.

questions.prompt: A prop letter must be read by the actor but not fully seen by the audience. Which design choice is sensible?
options: Write enough visible text for the actor and make the outside look believable
Leave the paper completely blank on both sides
Use a heavy metal sheet as the letter
Let the audience read it silently for ten minutes
questions.correctAnswer: Write enough visible text for the actor and make the outside look believable
questions.explanation: A practical prop supports performance needs while appearing convincing within the scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply prop design to support actor action and audience belief.

questions.prompt: An actor playing an elderly character uses a slightly slower walk, careful posture, and measured speech. Which technique is being applied?
options: Physical and vocal characterisation
Film exporting
Ticket pricing
Curtain repair
questions.correctAnswer: Physical and vocal characterisation
questions.explanation: Voice and body choices help portray age, health, mood, and social identity when used respectfully.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply physical and vocal choices to portray character.

questions.prompt: A film group records an interview beside a noisy road. Which action best improves sound quality?
options: Move to a quieter place or position the microphone closer to the speaker
Record farther away from the speaker
Ask the speaker to face away from the microphone
Ignore sound because pictures are enough
questions.correctAnswer: Move to a quieter place or position the microphone closer to the speaker
questions.explanation: Good location choice and microphone placement reduce unwanted noise and make dialogue clearer.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic sound recording practices to film production.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a poem line to create a strong image of drought. Which line best uses imagery for performance?
options: The cracked earth waits with an empty mouth
Drought is a topic in this poem
I will now talk about dry weather
There is no image here
questions.correctAnswer: The cracked earth waits with an empty mouth
questions.explanation: Imagery uses vivid language that helps listeners picture and feel the idea being performed.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply imagery to strengthen spoken word writing.

questions.prompt: A costume for a village elder needs to suggest dignity without copying sacred attire carelessly. Which approach is best?
options: Use respectful, general design clues and consult reliable cultural knowledge
Use any sacred item because it looks impressive
Mock the culture for comic effect
Choose unrelated sports uniform
questions.correctAnswer: Use respectful, general design clues and consult reliable cultural knowledge
questions.explanation: Cultural costume choices should be respectful, researched, and suited to the performance purpose.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply respectful costume design to culturally rooted performance.

questions.prompt: A director wants to show tension between two friends after a disagreement. Which staging choice best supports this?
options: Place them apart, avoid direct eye contact at first, then let distance change as they reconcile
Make them stand very close and laugh throughout
Have both face the back wall and freeze for the whole scene
Remove all movement and dialogue
questions.correctAnswer: Place them apart, avoid direct eye contact at first, then let distance change as they reconcile
questions.explanation: Distance, eye contact, and movement can reveal emotional relationships and changing conflict.
questions.learningOutcome: Use stage space to communicate relationship and conflict.

questions.prompt: A storyboard frame shows a learner looking nervously at an exam paper. Which shot best captures facial anxiety?
options: Close-up of the learner's face
Extreme wide shot from outside the school gate
Shot of an empty ceiling
Back view of a closed cupboard
questions.correctAnswer: Close-up of the learner's face
questions.explanation: A close-up is effective when the main purpose is to show facial expression and emotion.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable shots for communicating emotion in film.

questions.prompt: A play includes a short choral speaking section. Which rehearsal focus is most important?
options: Unified rhythm, clear articulation, and balanced voices
Individual actors shouting unrelated lines
Costume colour only
Camera angle only
questions.correctAnswer: Unified rhythm, clear articulation, and balanced voices
questions.explanation: Choral speaking depends on ensemble timing, shared rhythm, and clarity so the group sounds intentional.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ensemble speech skills in choral performance.

questions.prompt: A production team must inform learners about auditions. Which publicity method is most appropriate inside a school?
options: A clear notice with role requirements, venue, date, time, and contact person
A hidden note in a locked room
A rumour without audition details
A poster with no date or venue
questions.correctAnswer: A clear notice with role requirements, venue, date, time, and contact person
questions.explanation: Effective publicity gives practical information so interested participants know how to attend and prepare.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply clear communication when publicising a performance activity.

questions.prompt: During filming, an actor exits screen right in one shot. To maintain direction in the next shot, what should the actor generally do?
options: Enter from screen left if continuing the same movement across space
Enter from the same side without reason
Appear from the ceiling area
Stay outside the frame forever
questions.correctAnswer: Enter from screen left if continuing the same movement across space
questions.explanation: Screen direction helps viewers understand continuous movement from one shot to the next.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply screen-direction continuity in simple film scenes.

questions.prompt: A stage combat moment requires one actor to fall safely. Which practice is most suitable?
options: Choreograph the movement slowly, rehearse it safely, and use agreed cues
Let actors surprise each other during the show
Use real force to make it look true
Perform it without supervision or rehearsal
questions.correctAnswer: Choreograph the movement slowly, rehearse it safely, and use agreed cues
questions.explanation: Stage action that suggests danger must be carefully planned and rehearsed to protect performers.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety principles to staged physical action.

questions.prompt: A short film needs to show that two events happen at the same time in different locations. Which editing method is suitable?
options: Cross-cutting between the two locations
Repeating one still photograph only
Deleting all action from one location
Using unrelated shots of clouds only
questions.correctAnswer: Cross-cutting between the two locations
questions.explanation: Cross-cutting alternates between locations or actions to suggest simultaneity or comparison.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply cross-cutting to show parallel action.

questions.prompt: A performer often forgets lines after a cue. Which strategy is best for rehearsal?
options: Practise cue-to-line links and understand the intention behind each line
Memorise only isolated words without context
Avoid all run-throughs
Ask another actor to say every line
questions.correctAnswer: Practise cue-to-line links and understand the intention behind each line
questions.explanation: Lines are easier to retain when the performer knows the cue, action, and purpose of the speech.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply effective strategies for learning lines.

questions.prompt: A group wants to turn a news report about tree planting into drama. Which choice best avoids a lecture-like scene?
options: Create characters with goals and conflict around the tree planting issue
Read the report aloud without any dramatic action
List facts while standing still for ten minutes
Remove all character relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Create characters with goals and conflict around the tree planting issue
questions.explanation: Dramatic action needs characters, objectives, obstacles, and choices rather than only information delivery.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply dramatic structure to a social or environmental issue.

questions.prompt: A film crew has one afternoon to shoot a school scene. Which planning document best organises who is needed, where, and when?
options: Call sheet
Costume label only
Audience review
Final poster
questions.correctAnswer: Call sheet
questions.explanation: A call sheet gives cast and crew practical information such as schedule, location, roles, and contacts.
questions.learningOutcome: Use production documents to organise a simple film shoot.

questions.prompt: A scene should shift from comedy to serious reflection. Which performance choice best helps the shift?
options: Slow the pace, reduce playful movement, and use more focused vocal tone
Keep slapstick movement unchanged throughout
Ask the audience to ignore the change
Brighten every action without altering delivery
questions.correctAnswer: Slow the pace, reduce playful movement, and use more focused vocal tone
questions.explanation: Changes in pace, movement, and vocal tone can guide the audience into a new mood.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply performance choices to communicate changes in mood.

questions.prompt: A director asks actors to identify what their characters want in each scene. Which concept are they working on?
options: Objective
Lens focus
Seat plan
Budget balance
questions.correctAnswer: Objective
questions.explanation: A character objective is what the character wants to achieve and it drives action in the scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply character objectives to guide performance choices.

questions.prompt: A classroom performance uses a drumbeat from offstage to signal an approaching ceremony. What function does the sound serve?
options: Cueing atmosphere and offstage action
Replacing all character speech permanently
Showing the ticket price
Changing the school calendar
questions.correctAnswer: Cueing atmosphere and offstage action
questions.explanation: Sound can prepare the audience for action not yet visible and shape cultural or emotional atmosphere.
questions.learningOutcome: Use sound cues to support action and setting.

questions.prompt: A learner reviewing a performance says, 'The ending was effective because the actors formed a silent circle around the repaired water tap.' Which review skill is shown?
options: Using a specific performance detail to support judgement
Giving a vague opinion with no evidence
Ignoring the final stage image
Listing unrelated ticket prices
questions.correctAnswer: Using a specific performance detail to support judgement
questions.explanation: A strong review connects evaluation to observable details from the production.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply evidence-based judgement when reviewing a performance.

questions.prompt: A play about school bullying includes a comic teacher who distracts from the victim's experience. What is the strongest revision focus?
options: Balance humour with the seriousness of the theme and the character's journey
Add more unrelated jokes to every scene
Remove all conflict from the story
Ignore audience understanding
questions.correctAnswer: Balance humour with the seriousness of the theme and the character's journey
questions.explanation: Tone should serve the theme; misplaced comedy can weaken empathy and confuse the message.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how tone affects the communication of a performance theme.

questions.prompt: In a filmed argument, one actor looks screen left in close-up and the other also looks screen left in response. What problem may viewers experience?
options: They may seem to face the same direction instead of looking at each other
They will automatically understand the geography better
The scene will become a stage musical
The dialogue will become clearer because of eye-line mismatch
questions.correctAnswer: They may seem to face the same direction instead of looking at each other
questions.explanation: Eye-line continuity helps viewers understand spatial relationships during filmed dialogue.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse continuity problems in filmed conversation scenes.

questions.prompt: A performance about corruption uses only direct speeches to the audience and no character choices. What is the main dramatic weakness?
options: It tells the issue but lacks action, conflict, and transformation
It has too many believable character decisions
It overuses visual storytelling
It contains too much motivated silence
questions.correctAnswer: It tells the issue but lacks action, conflict, and transformation
questions.explanation: Drama becomes stronger when ideas are embodied through characters making choices under pressure.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the difference between message delivery and dramatic action.

questions.prompt: A stage scene places the most important conversation at the far corner while minor action happens centre stage. What is the likely issue?
options: Audience focus is pulled away from the main dramatic action
The set automatically becomes more realistic
The actors become louder without effort
The script becomes shorter
questions.correctAnswer: Audience focus is pulled away from the main dramatic action
questions.explanation: Blocking should guide attention to the most important action at each moment.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how stage composition affects audience focus.

questions.prompt: Two groups perform the same folktale. Group A copies narration exactly; Group B keeps the lesson but uses present-day school characters. Which judgement is strongest?
options: Group B shows adaptation because it transforms source material for a new context
Group A is always more creative because it changes nothing
Both groups have removed the original lesson completely
Group B cannot be theatre because it uses school characters
questions.correctAnswer: Group B shows adaptation because it transforms source material for a new context
questions.explanation: Adaptation may preserve core meaning while changing setting, characters, language, or structure for a target audience.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse approaches to adapting traditional material for contemporary performance.

questions.prompt: A film shows a learner studying late, then cuts to the same learner sleeping in class. What meaning does the edit most likely create?
options: A cause-and-effect link between late study and tiredness
A change to a completely unrelated character
A guarantee that no time has passed
A live stage entrance
questions.correctAnswer: A cause-and-effect link between late study and tiredness
questions.explanation: Editing can connect events so viewers infer cause, contrast, or consequence between shots.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how shot order creates meaning in film.

questions.prompt: A critic says the set was beautiful but never explains whether it supported the story. What is missing from the critique?
options: A link between design choices and dramatic purpose
A list of actor phone numbers
A longer description of ticket colours
A demand that every set be expensive
questions.correctAnswer: A link between design choices and dramatic purpose
questions.explanation: Useful critique evaluates how performance elements serve theme, character, mood, and audience understanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the quality of performance evaluation comments.

questions.prompt: A student actor uses a comic accent to represent a real Kenyan community and classmates laugh at the community rather than the character. What is the main ethical concern?
options: The performance may stereotype or disrespect a community
The scene has too much accurate research
The actor used clear articulation
The costume matched the character's occupation
questions.correctAnswer: The performance may stereotype or disrespect a community
questions.explanation: Performers should avoid choices that mock identities or reduce communities to harmful stereotypes.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ethical issues in character portrayal and representation.

questions.prompt: A monologue has strong words but the performer paces randomly and looks down throughout. What is the main performance gap?
options: Physical delivery does not support the spoken message
The words are automatically unimportant
The stage manager has no role
The audience should not see facial expression
questions.correctAnswer: Physical delivery does not support the spoken message
questions.explanation: Gesture, posture, eye focus, and movement should be chosen to strengthen the meaning of a monologue.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the relationship between physical delivery and spoken meaning.

questions.prompt: A short film uses loud background music during every dialogue scene, making words difficult to hear. What production judgement is best?
options: The sound mix should prioritise intelligible dialogue where speech carries meaning
Music should always be louder than speech
Dialogue is unnecessary in any school film
The scene needs more camera shake instead
questions.correctAnswer: The sound mix should prioritise intelligible dialogue where speech carries meaning
questions.explanation: Sound levels should serve storytelling; music supports mood but should not hide essential speech.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how sound balance affects film communication.

questions.prompt: A play has a strong opening and ending, but scenes in the middle repeat the same argument without change. What structural issue is present?
options: Weak progression of conflict and character development
Too much variety in objectives
Excessive resolution in every scene
Perfect escalation of dramatic action
questions.correctAnswer: Weak progression of conflict and character development
questions.explanation: Middle scenes should develop obstacles, choices, discoveries, or consequences rather than repeat the same beat.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse progression in dramatic structure.

questions.prompt: A production uses a real flame on stage to show a cooking scene in a school hall. What is the strongest safety judgement?
options: Replace it with a safe simulated effect and follow venue safety rules
Use the flame because realism is always more important
Ask the audience to sit closer to the flame
Ignore teacher supervision if actors are confident
questions.correctAnswer: Replace it with a safe simulated effect and follow venue safety rules
questions.explanation: School productions should prioritise safety and can use design alternatives to suggest dangerous actions.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate safety risks in school performance production.

questions.prompt: A film director wants viewers to feel trapped with a character in a narrow corridor. Which visual choice best supports that intention?
options: Tight framing with limited visible space around the character
A wide open field shot with no walls
Random shots of unrelated objects
Bright comedy lighting in every frame
questions.correctAnswer: Tight framing with limited visible space around the character
questions.explanation: Framing can create emotional meaning by controlling how much space viewers see around a character.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how framing choices create mood in film.

questions.prompt: A group uses call-and-response, song fragments, dance, and narration from an oral story in a stage piece. Which theatre influence is most evident?
options: Traditional African performance conventions
Silent spreadsheet formatting
Purely mechanical drawing
Unrelated laboratory procedure
questions.correctAnswer: Traditional African performance conventions
questions.explanation: Traditional African performance commonly integrates narration, music, movement, audience response, and communal storytelling.
questions.subStrandTitle: Traditional Kenyan Theatre and Performance Forms
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse features of traditional performance in contemporary staging.

questions.prompt: A review praises an actor's loud voice but notes that every emotion sounded angry. What acting issue is being identified?
options: Limited vocal range and emotional variation
Excellent contrast in tone
Accurate film continuity
Strong costume research only
questions.correctAnswer: Limited vocal range and emotional variation
questions.explanation: Effective acting uses varied vocal qualities to express different intentions, emotions, and moments of change.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse vocal performance in acting evaluation.

questions.prompt: A devised scene ends with a character suddenly changing behaviour without any earlier clue. What revision would best strengthen the performance?
options: Add motivated events or discoveries that make the change believable
Remove all earlier scenes
Make the change even more random
Tell the audience to accept it without evidence
questions.correctAnswer: Add motivated events or discoveries that make the change believable
questions.explanation: Character change is stronger when the audience can trace the causes through earlier action.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse motivation and consistency in character development.

questions.prompt: A stage design fills the acting area with large decorations so actors cannot move safely. What is the main design problem?
options: The set ignores performance space and safety needs
The set has too little decoration
The actors should not move in drama
The lighting will automatically solve the problem
questions.correctAnswer: The set ignores performance space and safety needs
questions.explanation: Set design should support action, visibility, safety, and meaning rather than block essential movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse practical constraints in stage design.

questions.prompt: A film scene begins with a close-up of a broken trophy before the character enters crying. What does this visual choice most likely do?
options: Foreshadows or symbolises the character's loss
Shows that the trophy is unrelated to the scene
Proves that no emotion will follow
Turns the scene into live theatre only
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadows or symbolises the character's loss
questions.explanation: An object shown before action can prepare meaning and carry symbolic importance in screen storytelling.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse symbolic use of objects in film scenes.

questions.prompt: A production budget spends almost all funds on posters but leaves no money for essential props and transport. What is the best evaluation?
options: The budget does not match production priorities and practical needs
The budget is balanced because publicity always comes first
The team should remove all planning documents
The production no longer needs performers
questions.correctAnswer: The budget does not match production priorities and practical needs
questions.explanation: Budget decisions should support the full production process, including rehearsal, performance resources, safety, and audience communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate whether a production budget supports stated performance needs.

questions.prompt: A school performance invites audience participation, but actors do not know how to continue after audience responses. What is the main preparation gap?
options: The group did not plan and rehearse rules for interaction
Audience participation can never work in theatre
The set should be more expensive
The scene needs no performer listening
questions.correctAnswer: The group did not plan and rehearse rules for interaction
questions.explanation: Interactive performance needs clear structure, performer flexibility, and boundaries so audience input supports the story.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse preparation needs for interactive performance.

questions.prompt: A team must create a five-minute performance on peaceful conflict resolution for Grade 10 learners. Which concept gives the strongest creative brief?
options: Two classmates compete for leadership, learn to listen, and resolve the conflict through mediated dialogue
Actors stand in a line and define peace from a dictionary
The group copies a random internet skit without permission
The performance has no conflict because peace is the theme
questions.correctAnswer: Two classmates compete for leadership, learn to listen, and resolve the conflict through mediated dialogue
questions.explanation: A strong brief gives characters, conflict, audience, theme, and a dramatic path for transformation.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a focused performance concept from a contemporary issue.

questions.prompt: You are designing a short film about examination pressure without using narration. Which plan best shows rather than tells the theme?
options: Use repeated shots of a ticking clock, unfinished notes, tense silence, and a calmer ending after asking for help
Open with a character explaining every message to camera
Place a title saying 'stress' on every shot
Remove all visual details and only list facts
questions.correctAnswer: Use repeated shots of a ticking clock, unfinished notes, tense silence, and a calmer ending after asking for help
questions.explanation: Film can communicate theme through images, sound, rhythm, and action instead of direct explanation.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a screen storytelling plan using visual and sound clues.

questions.prompt: A group needs to modernise a traditional trickster tale for a school festival while keeping its moral lesson. Which adaptation choice is strongest?
options: Set it in a student council campaign where cleverness has consequences and the original lesson remains clear
Change every event until the moral disappears
Use only costumes from the past with no performance choices
Avoid acknowledging that it came from oral tradition
questions.correctAnswer: Set it in a student council campaign where cleverness has consequences and the original lesson remains clear
questions.explanation: Effective adaptation transforms context while retaining the source's core conflict, lesson, and cultural respect.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an adaptation approach that preserves core meaning while updating context.

questions.prompt: A theatre group has ten performers but only three speaking roles. Which staging solution best uses the whole ensemble meaningfully?
options: Create chorus, movement, crowd, soundscape, and tableau roles that support the central action
Make seven performers sit backstage with no task
Give everyone the same lines at the same time throughout
Remove the main characters to create equal speaking time
questions.correctAnswer: Create chorus, movement, crowd, soundscape, and tableau roles that support the central action
questions.explanation: Ensemble creation can distribute meaningful performance work without weakening the story structure.
questions.learningOutcome: Design ensemble roles that support a performance concept.

questions.prompt: A production team is choosing between a realistic market set and a symbolic set of baskets, cloth, and sound cues. Which criterion should guide the decision?
options: Which design best supports theme, budget, safety, scene changes, and audience understanding
Which option uses the most objects regardless of meaning
Which option is hardest to move
Which option ignores the director's concept
questions.correctAnswer: Which design best supports theme, budget, safety, scene changes, and audience understanding
questions.explanation: Design evaluation should balance artistic meaning with practical production constraints.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate and select a stage design approach for a production concept.

questions.prompt: A class must produce a performance using a story from a community elder. Which plan best protects ethical practice?
options: Seek permission, record source details, represent the story respectfully, and credit the contributor
Use the story without asking because it is interesting
Change the elder's name and claim the story as original
Mock unfamiliar customs to make the audience laugh
questions.correctAnswer: Seek permission, record source details, represent the story respectfully, and credit the contributor
questions.explanation: Ethical performance practice values consent, attribution, respectful representation, and cultural responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate ethical steps when using community-sourced performance material.

questions.prompt: A five-shot film sequence must show a learner deciding to apologise after a quarrel. Which sequence has the clearest dramatic progression?
options: Quarrel, lonely reflection, memory of hurtful words, decision to write a message, meeting to apologise
Random school gate, empty desk, unrelated song, running feet, blank wall
Apology first, quarrel after, no reaction, unrelated poster, sudden ending
Five identical shots of the learner smiling
questions.correctAnswer: Quarrel, lonely reflection, memory of hurtful words, decision to write a message, meeting to apologise
questions.explanation: A coherent sequence shows conflict, reflection, decision, action, and resolution.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a shot sequence that communicates character change.

questions.prompt: A performance on climate action risks sounding like a lecture. Which creative strategy best makes it dramatic?
options: Build a story around characters whose choices about a polluted stream create conflict and consequences
Have each actor read a paragraph from a report without interaction
Project a list of facts and end immediately
Remove all obstacles so everyone agrees from the start
questions.correctAnswer: Build a story around characters whose choices about a polluted stream create conflict and consequences
questions.explanation: Thematic performance is stronger when ideas are embodied through character objectives, obstacles, and consequences.
questions.learningOutcome: Create dramatic action from a social or environmental theme.

questions.prompt: A group is evaluating whether their final rehearsal is ready for an audience. Which checklist is most complete?
options: Clear story, audible speech, safe movement, working cues, prepared props, respectful content, and timed running order
Only colourful costumes and loud music
Only ticket sales and food arrangements
Only the number of actors in the group
questions.correctAnswer: Clear story, audible speech, safe movement, working cues, prepared props, respectful content, and timed running order
questions.explanation: Readiness involves artistic clarity, technical coordination, safety, ethics, resources, and time management.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate production readiness before public presentation.

questions.prompt: You must design a fair rubric for assessing a Grade 10 group performance. Which set of criteria is strongest?
options: Creativity, performance skill, collaboration, technical support, theme clarity, safety, and reflection
Only volume of applause
Only the cost of costumes
Only how many lines each performer speaks
questions.correctAnswer: Creativity, performance skill, collaboration, technical support, theme clarity, safety, and reflection
questions.explanation: A fair rubric assesses several dimensions of both process and product, not just popularity or expense.
questions.learningOutcome: Create criteria for fair evaluation of a group performance.
